current.text: He is projected to start at guard with Maxey, Jaylen Brown, LeBron James and Embiid.
If the lineup does not fit, he is the starter most likely to move to the bench.
Experts expect him to be the third option, not the second. Usage could fall to about 18 to 20 percent, and his points and assists should drop with Brown, LeBron and a healthier Embiid around him.
Nick Nurse should still give him about 34 minutes, which keeps his steals strong.
Expect big ups and downs from week to week as Embiid, LeBron and others move in and out of the lineup.
Experts doubt he can match last season's top 70 finish. One sees a risk he ends up around 110th, but another says he will not fall as far as an ESPN ADP of 112.
Draft him in the 90s, not in the 60s or 70s. At around pick 104 he is a value.
In an auction he is worth about 10 USD. A price of 13 USD is too high.
Philadelphia plays 3-4-4 games in our playoff weeks (March 28 end) and has only 13 back-to-backs this season. One note says three of them fall in the fantasy playoffs.

durable.text: He beat expectations as a rookie. His ADP was 97 and he finished 62nd in category leagues. Late in the season he was top 50.
Steals are his best category. FG% is his weakest, a little below the pool.

note: The market already prices him low: Yahoo ranks him 86 and values him at 9 USD, ESPN at 7 USD, and average costs are only 4 to 5 USD. That fits the experts' range of picks in the 90s and about 10 USD, so pay up to about 10 USD and no more than that. He helps steals (z +1.7) and threes with a small FG% cost. Early in the season, check whether he stays in the starting five, plays about 34 minutes, and how much his usage and assists drop next to Brown and LeBron.
